section_summary.extract_value: This section presents Fig. 1, which displays three indirect effect path analysis models (Panels A, B, and C) examining the relationship between different body dissatisfaction predictors and body appreciation, mediated through body image flexibility. All three panels use the same sample (N = 84) and test different conceptualizations of body dissatisfaction: current minus personal ideal body size (Panel A), current minus cultural ideal body size (Panel B), and current minus typical female peer body size (Panel C). The figure demonstrates standardized beta coefficients for each pathway in the models.

Asset Caption.extract_value: Fig. 1. (Panel A) Indirect effect model with current minus personal ideal body size as the body dissatisfaction predictor (N = 84; β = −.34). (Panel B) Indirect effect model with current minus cultural ideal body size as the body dissatisfaction predictor (N = 84; β = −.33). (Panel C) Indirect effect model with current minus typical female peer body size as the body dissatisfaction predictor (N = 84; β = −.28). Note that all beta coefficients reported for these unadjusted models are standardized. *** p < .001, ** p < .01, * p < .05.
